messages:
cheng: Heads-up — since the us-west2 nodepool rollout last night we're seeing a steady trickle of small GPU pods getting stuck Pending and then flapping evictions. Rack-level placement looks skewed, NVLink counters spiked on a couple racks. Not sure if scheduler weights or the node labels got munged during the upgrade. Anyone else seeing this?

alex: I saw the alerts. Pods pending with reason=Unschedulable, but nodes claim capacity. Could be affinity/taint mismatch or leftover label `gpu.generation` differences.

platform-bot: autoscaler: scaled up warm-pool-us-west2 from 8 -> 12 at 02:04 UTC, reason=PodPendingForecast, events=5.

maria: Quick check — `kubectl get nodes -l topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-west2* -o wide` shows a subset of racks labelled `rack=R3` without `nvlink=true`. That would push packing to other racks. Did the rollout change the node-template?

cheng: @maria good catch. I grep'd the nodepool template and found a missing annotation `hardware.redwood.com/nvlink: "true"` on the newer instances. That explains why scheduler's rack affinity put more GPU pods onto fewer racks.

jordan: That plus our default binpacking score heavily weighting `rack` locality = high could create hot racks. NVLink saturation then causes slow heartbeats and kubelet evictions.

ops-oncall: Immediate mitigation — I'm going to taint the overloaded nodes with `gpu.hot=true:NoSchedule` for 10m to drain new pods away, and set priorityClass for critical serving jobs so they don't get preempted. Manual commands: ```bash
kubectl taint nodes node-abc gpu.hot=true:NoSchedule --overwrite
kubectl patch pod <critical-pod> -p '{"spec":{"priorityClassName":"redwood-critical"}}'
```

alex: For a medium-term fix we should (1) patch the nodepool templates to add the missing annotation, (2) run a rolling replace for affected instances, and (3) adjust scheduler scoring to factor nvlink capability rather than only rack label.

maria: Also we should update the model used by the binpacker — current cost function doesn't penalize NVLink saturation, only CPU/GPU counts. I can prototype adding a penality term from NIC/NVLink metrics.

platform-bot: telemetry: NVLink utilization (R3-rack-2) = 93% 1h avg, packet drops +15% vs baseline.

cheng: Cost note — if we don't reduce the hot-spotting, autoscaler will keep adding replacements and warm pool churn will cost ~+$12k/mo on us-west2 (estimate). Better to fix placement than overprovision.

jordan: Proposal: introduce a temporary scheduler predicate: prefer nodes with `hardware.redwood.com/nvlink=true` and add a cheap prefilter that rejects nodes with `nvlink_util>85%` for new allocations. Roll out as a canary in us-west2 only (5% of scheduling decisions) and monitor e2e latencies for GPU jobs.

maria: I'll open a PR for the scheduler change and the updated cost function. Will include a flag `--nvlink-aware` so it's togglable. Also adding an e2e eval comparing token-per-second for affected models.

ops-oncall: For the immediate window I've drained 4 nodes and pushed pods to other AZs. Eviction noise reduced. Keeping the taint for 20m.

alex: Long-term, we should protect nodepool templates with a unit-test in our infra repo that validates required hardware annotations before any pool rollout. Prevents this class of error.

cheng: Action items: @maria PR for scheduler + cost function (owner), @alex infra unit-test (owner), @ops-oncall keep taint for now and monitor (owner). Can we aim to have the canary merged and deployed in the next 24h?

jordan: I'll instrument metrics for `scheduler.assignment.nvlink_mismatch` and an alert when >5% new pods hit fallback racks.

maria: ACK — starting PR now. Will add perf numbers and the canary rollout plan.

cheng: Thanks — good triage. Follow-up in #eng-platform after PR review. :thumbsup:
